comment: The engine's allowed unsafe items (no-cliffs C-2c-ii scope r4 section 1.3): scripts/unsafe-inventory.mjs --check compares them with the tree. hash: sha256 of the item's tokens (its outer attributes included; comments and layout excluded). audit: the answer to the boundary question for that item; a new or changed item needs a fresh review and audit.

premises.external_proc_macros_audit: Trusted dependencies (scope r4: external crates and their macro expansions are the trusted boundary). The compiler sweep can't see their expansions (rustc treats them as external), so the exact name/version set is pinned: a new proc-macro dependency or a version change fails until reviewed.

engine/flint/build.rs.audit: Emits only cargo link directives (link-search, static/dylib libs); writes no Rust source and nothing is include!d. Test-only crate (never in a shipped graph).

engine/node/build.rs.audit: napi_build::setup() only: N-API link arguments; writes no Rust source, and engine/node has no include!.

premises.no_ledger_dep_audit: Checked per crate from its manifest (any dependency section, any name); with no re-export of sagebrush_ledger anywhere (also checked), a crate on this list cannot name a ledger type.
premises.compile_time_closure_audit: The trusted external-macro boundary (scope r4): code that generates or shapes our crates' code at build time, i.e. the external proc-macro crates, the members' build dependencies, and everything they depend on, pinned by name, version, source (crates.io only) and Cargo.lock checksum. Their expansions into our crates (pyo3/napi glue) are excluded from item enumeration only inside this pinned set; a new crate, a version, source or checksum change fails until reviewed.
premises.verified_toolchain_audit: The compiler sweep's coverage (force-warn reports local macro_rules, local proc-macro and include! expansions, but not external proc-macro glue) was verified on this compiler (VM1 controls K0-K4). A toolchain bump fails this check until those controls are re-run on the new compiler.
premises.compile_views: host --workspace --all-targets (minus the test-only FLINT crates); --all-features for ledger, interrupt, poly, py; wasm32 web, raster, growth-probe; x86_64-pc-windows-msvc interrupt. A declared set: a new cfg or target with unsafe-relevant code must be added to scripts/unsafe-sweep.sh.

items.item: impl Source for Borrowed > fn readable_within
items.audit: Can it produce or alter an Obligations, Operation, Reservation, Growth or Context (directly, generically or through a pointer)? No. libc::poll on one pollfd local to the call (the borrowed input descriptor, POLLIN), with a bounded millisecond timeout; it reads and writes only that local and returns a count. No ledger object is involved.

Can it produce or alter an Obligations, Operation, Reservation, Growth or Context (directly, generically or through a pointer)? No. It wraps a descriptor (POSIX) or handle (Windows) that the caller owns in a File held in ManuallyDrop, so the File is never closed here; the request loop only reads and writes bytes through it. It touches no ledger object and is not generic over one.

Can it produce or alter an Obligations, Operation, Reservation, Growth or Context (directly, generically or through a pointer)? No. MainThread holds a pthread_t, only ever passed to pthread_kill by the control thread (a pointer type on macOS, hence not Send by default). Sending the id across threads shares no memory. No ledger type is involved.

Can it produce or alter an Obligations, Operation, Reservation, Growth or Context (directly, generically or through a pointer)? No. pthread_self() returns the calling thread's id, wrapped for the control thread's wake. It has no preconditions and no effect.

Can it produce or alter an Obligations, Operation, Reservation, Growth or Context (directly, generically or through a pointer)? No. sigaction with a null new action only reads SIGUSR1's current action (into a zeroed local); pthread_kill sends SIGUSR1 to the worker's main thread when that action is a handler. It reads and writes no memory but the local, and touches no ledger object.

Can it produce or alter an Obligations, Operation, Reservation, Growth or Context (directly, generically or through a pointer)? No. PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8 reads exactly line.len() bytes of the borrowed request line (valid for the call), with the GIL held; it returns a new str reference or NULL with an exception set, which Bound::from_owned_ptr_or_err takes over. It creates a Python str only; no ledger object.
